newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX says July foreign deliveries at 805,000 bbls.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX says July foreign deliveries at 805,000 bbls.

text.p: Foreign crude deliveries against the July NYMEX futures contract tallied 805,000 barrels out of a grand total of 1.271 million barrels delivered, a NYMEX official said Monday.
The foreign crude levels dipped considerably from recent months, reflecting absorption of crude overhang in the U.S. Gulf on active refiner buying, crude traders said.
Market players have said that Amoco picked up some of the Nigerian Bonny Light which had been in the hands of trading house J. Aron, eliminating much of the redeliverable supply.
"The delivered crude was mostly Nigerian Bonny Light," said a crude trader. "This should help keep the Exchange for Physicals down (weaker)."

Traders had expected some one million barrels of foreign crude to be redelivered, half Nigerian Bonny Light and half Norwegian Oseberg. The remaining deliverable crude was believed to be mainly in the hands of Arco, traders said.
The foreign crude began to appear on the exchange with the expiry of the May contract in April, when a record 2.73 million barrels of foreign supply was delivered.
Some of that record amount was redelivered along with fresh barrels on the June paper contract, which saw 2.349 million barrels of foreign delivered.

Foreign delivery fears have kept EFPs at a premium to the NYMEX price. EFPs, which allow traders to get out of paper positions to avoid getting stuck with alternative foreign crude, were around a five cents premium for August on Monday.
July EFPs, mirroring a trend for June, held as much as a 25 cents premium before demand died down, and deals were done at only a few pennies over the screen on Friday.
